title: OptionButton PopupMenu being overridden by hidden engine-level scroll container
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in Godot 4.6, 4.6.1 ### System information Windows 11, Forward+, RTX 5070 Ti ### Issue description - A hidden ScrollContainer node that the engine creates on runtime is overriding the OptionButton's PopupMenu child settings - I created a theme with customization for OptionButton and PopupMenu using distinct colors to see each node and specific area of the menu. The individual items of the dropdown menu were controllable with a Panel StyleBoxFlat, until I added ScrollContainer to the theme - Even if I used a theme variation for the ScrollBox that the drop down optionbutton was in, it still couldn't fix the underlying hidden ScrollContainer that shows up in Remote upon running the project - This demonstrates that no matter what you set in your .tres Theme, it will be incorrectly overrided by the underlying engine's default scrollcontainer theme and be unable to be corrected or fixed ### Expected Behavior The internal `ScrollContainer` should default to an empty/transparent StyleBox to prevent overriding the dropdown menu ### Actual Behavior The internal `ScrollContainer` uses the base `ScrollContainer` type, causing global styles to override `OptionButton` and `PopupMenu` configurations. **Potential Workaround:** - The only way around this I found was making a custom variation in the theme .tres 'ScrollContainerOuter' and assigning that variation to the scrollcontainer I have in my scene tree, and setting ScrollContainer itself to a styleboxempty. This essentially sets an empty scroll container, rendering the hidden engine-level one invisible This worked in my current project, but even in the MRP as I was testing, it seemed to break and become irreparable, getting stuck on a 'green' color I couldn't find nor get rid of. ### Steps to reproduce 1. **Create Scene:** Add an OptionButton to a scene. 2. **Populate Items:** Add 3+ items to the OptionButton via Inspector or script. 3. **Create Theme:** Create a new .tres Theme resource and assign it to the OptionButton. 4. **Configure OptionButton/PopupMenu:** * Add OptionButton to Theme. Set a StyleBoxFlat (Color A). * Add PopupMenu to Theme. Set a StyleBoxFlat (Color B) to the panel property. 5. **Configure ScrollContainer:** * Add ScrollContainer type to the Theme. * Assign a StyleBoxFlat with a high-contrast color (e.g., Green) to the panel property. 6. **Run Project:** Execute the scene. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [mrp-dropdown-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26376850/mrp-dropdown-bug.zip)
